## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `ordering-slack-conditioned-urgency`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-27T12:56:49.162Z.

Catalog entry, slug ordering-slack-conditioned-urgency, recorded 2026-07-27 by slug per the pm-g8t7b9 ordinal-collision rule. The catalog runs (1)-(28) and is not restarted here.

Gap this closes. Every scoring signal in the catalog answers a question about an item in isolation or about its similarity to the request: recency, affinity, structural position, outcome distance, evidence half-life. None answers the scheduling question, which is what it costs the project if this particular item waits. Two items can be equally relevant to what an agent is doing and have completely different consequences for delay: one sits on the only path to a dated milestone and every day it waits moves the milestone, the other has six weeks of float. Relevance treats them identically today. The outcome-distance-prior entry is the closest neighbour and is explicitly not this: it measures how far an item is from an outcome, which is a distance in the reachability graph, whereas this measures how much freedom the schedule has to defer it, which is a quantity in the ordering graph.

The algorithm. Over the ordering DAG, compute for each node the standard critical-path quantities: earliest start from predecessors, latest start from the deadline of every outcome it can reach, and slack as their difference. Convert slack to an urgency multiplier that is monotone decreasing and saturating, so zero-slack work is strongly promoted, moderate float is neutral, and very large float does not become a penalty that buries legitimate exploratory work. Multiply into the existing composite score rather than adding, so it modulates relevance instead of competing with it. Condition the multiplier on the requester: an agent working toward a specific target uses slack computed against that target's deadline, and an agent with no declared target uses the workspace-wide minimum over reachable outcomes.

Degeneracy, which is the acceptance condition every catalog entry has to state. In a workspace with no ordering edges, every node has infinite slack, the multiplier saturates to one everywhere, and the score is byte-identical to the score without this entry. That is the correct behaviour and it is also this workspace today: 664 of 9,502 edges carry sequence and 1,765 of 2,007 ordered nodes have no predecessor, so the entry would currently be a no-op and must be shown to be one. In a workspace with no deadlines the same thing happens through a different route, because latest-start is undefined and the entry declines rather than inventing a horizon.

Cost and scale. Slack is one forward and one backward topological pass, linear in edges, and it is recomputed only when the ordering graph or a deadline changes, which is far less often than items change. At million-item scale the passes run over the ordering projection alone, which is a small fraction of all edges, and the per-request cost is a table lookup. The small end degenerates as described rather than through a special-cased branch.

Dependencies and honesty constraint. This entry is unusable until the ordering graph is non-degenerate, so it is gated on pm-gxs55a rather than on any packer or store work, and it must never be allowed to create pressure to manufacture ordering edges in order to make itself useful. The 2026-07-27 extraction tranche under pm-ye46ns found ten honest precedence statements in the whole corpus, which is the measure of how far away that is. Forecast distributions from pm-uey8od are the natural upgrade: slack computed against a probabilistic completion date rather than a point deadline, with the multiplier taking the probability of the item becoming critical rather than a binary.

Scope clarification from individual-ownership review: pm-uey8od owns a related measurement, read primitive or defect fix. It does not independently deliver this proposed ranking behavior. Reuse its evidence and public API; evaluate the additional behavior in this experiment.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
